about: An unmatched word forwarded as an external command plus the rest of argv. clap's allow_external_subcommands: known subcommands still win, default_subcommand still catches first, and a flag-like token on the parent is still an unknown flag rather than a forwarded name.

vectors.doc: Once an unmatched word is taken as the external name, every token after it is forwarded with it, including flags.
A word that names a declared subcommand selects it; the catch-all is only for words that name nothing.
A flag-like token on the parent is still an unknown flag. This is clap's allow_external_subcommands, not unknown_flags=value.
A global flag typed before the unmatched word still binds on the parent; flags after it are forwarded.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
external_subcommand #true
flag "-v --verbose" global=#true
cmd "install"

vectors.doc: A declared default_subcommand already says what an unmatched word means, so it catches before the external forwarding.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
default_subcommand "run"
external_subcommand #true
cmd "run" {
  arg "[TASK]"
}

vectors.doc: A negative number is a value, not a flag, so it can be the unmatched word the catch-all forwards. usage-lib used to treat every token that starts with `-` as a flag and skip this path.
The property is per command: a nested cmd can forward while the root still owns its flags.
